title: Print and Comments
content:
What problem does this solve?
You need a way to see what your program is doing. print() sends text to the console so you can observe values while you learn.

Basic syntax
  print(value)
  print(value1, value2)

What actually happens
When Python reaches a print() call, it converts each argument to text, joins them with spaces by default, writes that text to standard output, then continues with the next line.

Comments start with #. Python ignores them entirely — they are notes for humans, not instructions for the computer.
concepts: print() writes values to the console
Multiple arguments to print are separated by spaces
Lines starting with # are comments and do not run

examples.title: A simple greeting
examples.explanation: Python evaluates the string, then print writes it followed by a newline.

examples.title: Comments explain intent
examples.code:
# Show the starting gold amount
print("Gold:", 50)
examples.explanation: The comment is skipped. print receives two arguments and inserts a space between them.

common_mistakes: Forgetting quotes around text: print(Hello) looks for a variable named Hello
Expecting comments to change program behavior — they never do

exercises.title: Greet the adventurer
exercises.prompt:
Write a program that prints exactly:
Hello, Adventurer!

Use print and a string.
hints: print() needs parentheses, and text needs quotes.
Use double or single quotes around the whole message.
A working shape is: print("Hello, Adventurer!")

exercises.prompt: What does the following program print? Type the exact output (no quotes).
hints: print joins multiple arguments with a single space.
There is no extra punctuation added between HP: and 100.
